# ring

```go
import "github.com/kitsunium/sdk/pkg/v1/collections/ring"
```

Package ring is a bounded, lock-free queue for exactly ONE producer and exactly ONE consumer: a fixed number of slots, a write that refuses when they are full, and a read that refuses when they are empty — neither ever blocks.

```
q, err := ring.New[Record](1024)

// The producer's goroutine — and only that one — writes.
if err := q.TryWrite(rec); errors.Is(err, ring.Full) {
    dropped++ // the caller's policy: drop, retry, or block upstream
}

// The consumer's goroutine — and only that one — reads.
rec, err := q.TryRead()
if errors.Is(err, ring.Empty) {
    // nothing yet: wait on a signal, never spin
}
```

It is the buffer behind the SDK's asynchronous logger, published as an alias of that kernel package (ADR 0159 §4).

### When to use it

Between one goroutine that produces on a hot path and one that consumes, when a full buffer must be an answer rather than a wait — a log record or a metric that the producer would rather drop than stall for. Two atomic loads and a store per operation, no lock and no allocation: an error is one of three sentinels, never built on the fly.

For anything else a buffered channel is the right tool: it blocks, it wakes the reader, and it takes any number of producers and consumers.

### One producer, one consumer — a precondition, not a hint

EXACTLY ONE goroutine may call TryWrite at a time, and EXACTLY ONE may call TryRead. Concurrent producers, or concurrent consumers, corrupt the queue: serialise them upstream, or take the multi-producer sibling.

### Many producers, one consumer

[NewMulti](#NewMulti) returns a [MultiQueue](#MultiQueue): the same four methods, under the wider contract of any number of goroutines calling TryWrite at once and exactly one calling TryRead. Its capacity is rounded up to a power of two. A writer claims a slot, then stores into it: while it is between the two, the reader answers [Empty](#Empty) for that slot and every one behind it. Publishing [Queue](#Queue) froze its four methods, so this mode arrived as another constructor and a sibling interface (ADR 0039, ADR 0159 §2).

### Errors

[Full](#Full) answers a TryWrite on a full ring, [Empty](#Empty) a TryRead on an empty one, and [CapZero](#CapZero) a [New](#New) with a capacity that is not positive. Each is a fixed value, matched with errors.Is or the SDK's errs.HasCode.

```go
var CapZero *errs.Error
```

CapZero is returned by New for a capacity that is not positive: a ring that can hold nothing is a configuration mistake, not a queue.

Initialised with `github.com/kitsunium/sdk/internal/kernel/collections/ring.CapZero`.

Code `0.1.3.3` · reason `RING_CAP_ZERO` · public "Ring buffer capacity must be positive"

<a name="Empty"></a>
```go
var Empty *errs.Error
```

Empty is returned by TryRead when no item is waiting; the caller decides whether to wait on a signal or yield — never to spin.

Initialised with `github.com/kitsunium/sdk/internal/kernel/collections/ring.Empty`.

Code `0.1.3.2` · reason `RING_EMPTY` · public "Ring buffer is empty"

<a name="Full"></a>
```go
var Full *errs.Error
```

Full is returned by TryWrite when every slot is taken; the caller decides whether to drop, retry or slow its producer.

Initialised with `github.com/kitsunium/sdk/internal/kernel/collections/ring.Full`.

<a name="Drain"></a>
## func [Drain](<https://github.com/kitsunium/sdk/blob/main/pkg/v1/collections/ring/gen_facade.go>)

```go
func Drain[T any](q Queue[T]) iter.Seq[T]
```

Drain yields the items q holds, oldest first, until it is empty — the consumer's TryRead loop as an iterator. Only the one consumer goroutine may range over it; a loop that breaks early leaves the rest in q.

<a name="New"></a>
## func [New](<https://github.com/kitsunium/sdk/blob/main/pkg/v1/collections/ring/gen_facade.go>)

```go
func New[T any](capacity int) (Queue[T], error)
```

New returns an empty [Queue](#Queue) holding at most capacity items, or [CapZero](#CapZero) when capacity is not positive. The storage is allocated once, here.

<details><summary>Example</summary>
<p>

ExampleNew hands items from one side to the other: a write past the capacity is refused, and reading stops at the first Empty.

```go
q, err := ring.New[string](2)
if err != nil {
	fmt.Println(err)
	return
}
for _, item := range []string{"first", "second", "third"} {
	if err := q.TryWrite(item); err != nil {
		fmt.Println(item, "refused, full:", errors.Is(err, ring.Full))
	}
}
for {
	item, err := q.TryRead()
	if err != nil {
		fmt.Println("then empty:", errors.Is(err, ring.Empty))
		return
	}
	fmt.Println(item)
}
```

#### Output

```
third refused, full: true
first
second
then empty: true
```

</p>
</details>

## type [MultiQueue](<https://github.com/kitsunium/sdk/blob/main/pkg/v1/collections/ring/gen_facade.go>)

MultiQueue is the multi-producer, single-consumer ring: TryWrite from any number of goroutines at once, TryRead from exactly one. The methods are [Queue](#Queue)'s, so a MultiQueue is also a Queue — [Drain](#Drain) reads it.

```go
type MultiQueue[T any] = kring.MultiQueue[T]
```

MultiQueue is an alias of `github.com/kitsunium/sdk/internal/kernel/collections/ring.MultiQueue`, declared as:

```go
type MultiQueue[T any] interface {
	Capacity() (n int)
	Len() (n int)
	TryRead() (item T, err error)
	TryWrite(item T) (err error)
}
```

<a name="MultiQueue.TryRead"></a>
### func \(MultiQueue\) [TryRead](<https://github.com/kitsunium/sdk/blob/main/internal/kernel/collections/ring/multi.go>)

```go
func (MultiQueue) TryRead() (item T, err error)
```

TryRead dequeues the next item without blocking; returns Empty when no item is available, including while the writer that claimed the next slot has not finished storing into it. One goroutine only.

<a name="MultiQueue.TryWrite"></a>
### func \(MultiQueue\) [TryWrite](<https://github.com/kitsunium/sdk/blob/main/internal/kernel/collections/ring/multi.go>)

```go
func (MultiQueue) TryWrite(item T) (err error)
```

TryWrite enqueues item without blocking; returns Full when saturated. Any number of goroutines may call it at once.

<a name="Queue"></a>
## type [Queue](<https://github.com/kitsunium/sdk/blob/main/pkg/v1/collections/ring/gen_facade.go>)

Queue is the single-producer, single-consumer ring.

TryWrite enqueues an item without blocking, or returns [Full](#Full). TryRead dequeues the oldest item without blocking, or returns [Empty](#Empty); the slot it read is cleared, so the queue keeps no reference to an item it handed out. Capacity is the number of items the ring holds when full, fixed at [New](#New). Len is a snapshot count — the producer or the consumer may move it before the caller acts on it.

Its four methods are frozen: a published interface grows by a sibling, never by a fifth method (ADR 0039).

```go
type Queue[T any] = kring.Queue[T]
```

```go
	Capacity() (n int)
	Len() (n int)

	TryWrite(item T) (err error)
}
```
